title: IDF hello_world
note: boots the ROM, prints, reboots through the watchdog

title: Touch-LCD-4B energy panel
note: LVGL 480x480 over the RGB bus, GT911 touch — swipe between pages; demo data from energydata.json, tiles toggle; the SID player is on the last page (enable audio)

title: …with the SID player playing
note: same firmware, a script swipes to the SID page and presses play at 5.5 s

title: ESP32-C3 · hello_world (RISC-V)
note: the other chip: one RV32IMC core, console only — real mask ROM through the bootloader into FreeRTOS. Verified line-for-line against a physical C3.

title: ESP32-C6 · hello_world (RISC-V)
note: the newest chip: one RV32IMAC core, console only — real mask ROM through the bootloader into FreeRTOS. Verified line-for-line against a Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47.

title: ESP32-C6 · 802.15.4 energy scanner
note: the Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47: LVGL spectrum of channels 11–26 on the ST7789 over SPI2 and DMA, the WS2812 blinking per scan, energy detect from the emulated 802.15.4 MAC with a moving 2.4 GHz picture — press BOOT for single-channel mode

title: ESP32-C6 · Contiki-NG
note: Contiki-NG on the ESP32-C6 as an unmodified IDF app: its own scheduler, CSMA and 802.15.4 stack over the emulated MAC, broadcasting every 5 s and blinking the WS2812 through the RMT

title: …two of them on one radio medium
note: two emulated C6 motes on one 802.15.4 medium, in this tab, with no simulator behind them: each hears the other's broadcasts. The second powers on 1.3 s later — two identical images booted together stay deterministic to the cycle and every frame collides

title: …an RPL/IPv6 network: root and client
note: two emulated C6 motes in this tab: node 1 is Contiki-NG's rpl-udp server and the DAG root, node 2 the client — it joins the DAG, then sends a UDP request every 10 s and gets a reply. 6LoWPAN, RPL Lite and CSMA end to end over the emulated 802.15.4 MAC, hardware ACKs included

title: Atech 14-port Pocket Synth
note: Arduino firmware on the 14-port board: ST7735 display, WS2812 ring, encoder and buttons, SID-chip synth — the script plays it (enable audio)

title: …as a C64 SID jukebox
note: same firmware: cRSID emulates a whole C64 — 6502, SID, CIA, VIC — so it plays real .sid tunes. Commando by Rob Hubbard, then Wizball (enable audio)
